No benchmark isolates whether an agent can design training algorithms. We present AI4AI-Bench, ten frozen repositories for evaluating algorithmic design.

1 Introduction

Existing suites cannot distinguish changes to run execution from changes to how a model learns, which prevents direct measurement of algorithmic design.

2 AI4AI-Bench

2.3 Protocol

Exploration is the same everywhere. For four hours the agent works inside the repository on one B300 and consults the fast proxy metric. When time is up, nothing else crosses forward: only the source.

The submitted source is executed from initialization until it terminates or twelve hours elapse, and the resulting checkpoints are scored.

The final metric is computed afterwards by an evaluator frozen before the first run, so the agent cannot access the metric that decides its result.

2.5 Scoring

Each task uses a progress coordinate \varphi with three reference points: the uninformative model x_{\perp}, the baseline, and the optimum.

The two branches meet at 0.1: matching the repository baseline is the pivot, what lies below it measures the distance from an uninformative model, and what lies above it measures progress to the optimum.

3 Experiments

3.2 Results

The mean score over the 290 cells is 0.166, the strongest system averages 0.250, and the single best configuration averages 0.288.

4 Analysis

4.1 Execution-level and learning-level changes

Four change how this run goes: run duration and saving, the training hyperparameters, checkpoint selection, and trainable capacity. Four change how the model learns: the loss it optimizes, the supervision signal, the update rule, and the data it trains on.

Submissions that touch the learning procedure average 0.226 against 0.126 for those that stay on the run side, a gap of 0.100.

4.2 Reasoning effort

The share of submissions that touch the learning algorithm rises from 8\% to 64\%.

The mean score rises from 0.094 at the lowest level to 0.196 at the highest.
